task.description: You are on branch feature/WF03-ISS0392-20260901 (checkout/pull it first). Read step-01-issue-fixer.json's result.summary in full -- ISSUE-FIXER's independently-confirmed diagnosis is your starting point, not ISS-0392.yaml's own narrative (though you may also read that record). Design a fix for the Ecto.Multi :task_records key collision. The collision: build_complete_task_tail_multi/6 (lib/letflow/engine.ex) unconditionally appends TaskActivation.append_multi_from_existing_records(parent_instance_id, ...) keyed {:task_records, parent_instance_id} at engine.ex:2415, then (when the hop chain enters a SUB_PROCESS node) calls through to SubProcess.append_start_multi/7 (lib/letflow/engine/sub_process.ex), whose maybe_chain_synchronous_completion/6 :completed clause (sub_process.ex:481-508, firing ONLY on a synchronously-completing child graph) calls build_completion_write_steps/12 which appends ANOTHER TaskActivation.append_multi_from_existing_records(parent_instance_id, ...) at sub_process.ex:966-972 -- keyed identically, causing Ecto.Multi.merge_results/3 to raise. This must also correctly handle maybe_cascade_to_grandparent/6 (sub_process.ex:1003+), which recurses this same append pattern per distinct ancestor instance_id in a multi-level SUB_PROCESS nesting -- each ancestor's OWN collision must be prevented without suppressing a distinct ancestor's legitimate step. Produce a design (no implementation code) in lib/letflow/design/iss0392-multi-task-records-collision-fix.md covering: (1) the exact mechanism the fix uses to avoid appending {:task_records, X} twice for the same X within one Multi -- e.g. a signature/contract change to accept the already-built Multi and skip/merge the duplicate step, or a check-before-append; state which of the involved functions' signatures change and how (name, new/changed params, return shape) -- no function bodies; (2) how the fix preserves the async/queued SUB_PROCESS completion path's existing behavior unchanged (ISS-0392's AC3); (3) how a multi-level cascade (grandparent, great-grandparent, ...) is handled so each ancestor's step is added exactly once; (4) the exact collision-triggering scenario the regression test must reproduce (a synchronously-completing START->END child graph spawned mid-hop-chain) so TEST-DESIGNER can build it directly from your design; (5) any open questions, listed explicitly rather than silently resolved by guessing.
acceptance_criteria: Design lives at lib/letflow/design/iss0392-multi-task-records-collision-fix.md, no function bodies/implementation code

Design maps to ISS-0392's 3 acceptance criteria exactly (no more raising on sync-completing child; regression test scenario named precisely; async/queued path behavior unchanged) with a concrete design element for each
Design states which function signatures change (if any) with exact new/changed parameter and return shapes
Design explicitly addresses the multi-level cascade case (maybe_cascade_to_grandparent/6) so it is not silently left ambiguous
No TBD/deferral language on anything CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR would treat as an unresolved acceptance criterion -- open questions are listed as such explicitly, not hidden

result.summary: Design lives at lib/letflow/design/iss0392-multi-task-records-collision-fix.md (design/prose only, no .ex bodies -- grepped the file for 'def ' followed by a `do` block spanning real logic and found none; the fenced @spec blocks are type signatures only). Read ISSUE-FIXER's full diagnosis (step-01-issue-fixer.json result.summary) plus lib/letflow/engine.ex:2380-2600, lib/letflow/engine/sub_process.ex (moduledoc, :380-519, :695-1063), and lib/letflow/engine/task_activation.ex in full directly -- not from the diagnosis prose alone -- and confirmed the exact call sites, key shapes and existing moduledoc rationale ('namespaced by instance_id ... so calls for DIFFERENT instance_ids can coexist', task_activation.ex:233-240) that the fix extends. Mechanism (design SS2): a new gatekeeper, TaskActivation.append_multi_from_existing_records_once/7, taking/returning an explicit MapSet.t(Ecto.UUID.t()) claimed-instance-ids accumulator threaded alongside the Multi through every function on the path from build_complete_task_tail_multi/6 down to the two existing append_multi_from_existing_records/6 call sites (engine.ex:2584, sub_process.ex:966-972) -- both direct calls are replaced with the gatekeeper. On a same-instance_id repeat within one transaction the gatekeeper REPLACES the earlier {:task_records, instance_id} step with the later one rather than skipping it, per SS2.3's dominance argument (the later, sub-process-completion-path call's previous_pending_task_nodes/new_instance_state snapshot strictly dominates the earlier hop-chain-only call's, because load_parent_context/2 re-reads the parent's current committed row state -- sub_process.ex:719 -- rather than reusing any in-memory value the earlier call had). Signature changes (SS2.5, all no-body @specs in the design doc): build_task_activation_and_reconciliation_multi/3->/4, append_sub_process_children_creation_multi/6->/7, SubProcess.append_start_multi/7->/8, maybe_chain_synchronous_completion/6->/7, append_completion_multi/5->/6 (success return changes {:ok, Multi.t()} -> {:ok, {Multi.t(), MapSet.t()}}), build_completion_write_steps/12->/13, maybe_cascade_to_grandparent/6->/7 -- every one gains one added claimed_instance_ids parameter and changes its Multi.t() return to a {Multi.t(), MapSet.t()} pair (error returns unchanged). append_multi_from_existing_records/6 itself (the fixed-atom-key variant used by Engine.create/2) is explicitly left unmodified. Cascade (SS3): maybe_cascade_to_grandparent/7 is covered by the same replace-by-recency rule -- each ancestor's instance_id is a distinct MapSet member/Multi key by construction (find_waiting_parent_token/3 resolves one specific ancestor per level), so one ancestor's step is never suppressed by another's; a same-instance-as-its-own-ancestor edge case is analyzed (SS3) and shown to still resolve correctly under 'most recently attempted wins', then explicitly flagged as OQ-4 since it may be unreachable under current graph validation and is not in ISS-0392's filed scope. Async/queued path (AC3, SS4): the no-op sibling clause of maybe_chain_synchronous_completion/7 (sub_process.ex:510-518 today) is shown to return {multi, claimed_instance_ids} completely unchanged -- arity changes but behavior is provably identical, since the whole fix is confined to the :completed-matching clause's downstream calls. Regression scenario (SS5): exact fixture (parent START->HUMAN_TASK('gate')->SUB_PROCESS('sp')->END, child START->END with no task) matching ISSUE-FIXER's own scratch/iss0392_repro_test.exs shape, pre-fix-must-raise / post-fix-must-succeed stated explicitly per WF-03's fail-then-pass rule, plus a second nested-cascade variant (outer SUB_PROCESS wrapping the first fixture as its own child) for multi-level coverage. Four open questions listed explicitly in SS6 (OQ-1: how the MapSet crosses a Multi.merge/2 callback boundary, given Ecto constrains that callback to return a bare Multi.t() -- two legitimate resolutions named, left to ELIXIR-DEV/REVIEWER; OQ-2: MapSet vs plain list for the accumulator, left to ELIXIR-DEV's judgment as behaviorally equivalent; OQ-3: whether the gatekeeper's replace behavior needs its own unit test beyond SS5's integration scenario, left to TEST-DESIGNER/TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR; OQ-4: the self-referential-ancestor edge case, flagged rather than assumed in or out of scope) -- none resolved by silent guessing, all named so ELIXIR-DEV/TEST-DESIGNER cannot discover an unstated assumption mid-build.
